ui.title: Factories from the Shinkansen
ui.description: Coffee, sweets and cosmetics: spot the factories beside the Tokaido Shinkansen with photographs and A-side and E-side window guides.
ui.deck: Coffee, sweets, cosmetics. The places that make everyday favourites line the tracks.
ui.left: On the left in the direction of travel
ui.right: On the right in the direction of travel
ui.nearby: More to look for on this section
ui.candidateIntro: These factories lie close to the tracks on the map. We are still checking what can be identified from today's trains.
ui.seatsText: A and E refer to the window seats in ordinary-class cars with 3+2 seating. Toward Shin-Osaka, A is on the left and E on the right; toward Tokyo, A is on the right and E on the left. In Green Cars, the D-seat window is on the same side as ordinary-class E. The seat letters stay on the same side of the line when the direction changes.
ui.notesTitle: About the guide and its sources
ui.notesText: Roles and products were checked against sources for each site, including company information, in November 2026. A product on a sign is not necessarily made at that factory. The guide also includes Suzuki's headquarters on the former Takatsuka factory site and Yanmar's research centre. Places are grouped by station section, not in exact passing order within each section. Distances are approximate; train speed and light affect the view. Sources marked “Japanese” are in Japanese.

ui.book: 栗原景『東海道新幹線の車窓は、こんなに面白い！』 — Toyo Keizai, 2016 (Japanese original)
ui.cta: Choose your train for a window guide
ui.comparisonCaption: About 800 m south of Nagoya Station, a roughly 70 m advertisement runs along the Market Square Sasashima shopping complex. Look on the A-seat side: left before reaching Nagoya toward Shin-Osaka, or right after leaving Nagoya toward Tokyo.
ui.observation: Train-window photo of the wind turbines (2025)
ui.comparisonAlt: A large white SINFONIA name on a green band along a white commercial building in Sasashima, Nagoya.
ui.entry: Spot the factories behind everyday drinks, sweets and cosmetics from your Shinkansen window.

fuji-area: At the foot of Mount Fuji

ucc.name: UCC Fuji Factory
ucc.hook: A coffee tower beneath Mount Fuji
ucc.point: Look for “UCC COFFEE FUJI” on the white tower. Mount Fuji rises behind this factory, which makes roasted coffee.
ucc.alt: A white tower marked UCC COFFEE FUJI, with Mount Fuji behind it.
ucc.related: More views of Mount Fuji from the train
sources: UCC: coffee production at the Fuji Factory (Japanese)

fuji.name: Nippon Paper Fuji Mill, Fuji site
fuji.point: Red-and-white chimneys with Mount Fuji behind them mark the site. Crecia-Kasuga's Shin-Fuji Mill, within the grounds, makes household paper such as toilet rolls.
fuji.alt: Chimneys and buildings at Nippon Paper's Fuji site spread out below Mount Fuji.
sources: Nippon Paper: Fuji Mill (Japanese)
Nippon Paper Crecia: production sites (Japanese)

koa.name: Koa Kogyo Head Office Factory
koa.hook: A rainbow above the mill at night
koa.point: This mill makes paper for corrugated cardboard and other uses. The rainbow illumination pictured belongs to a special display for 11–23 November 2026. It is not a regular sight.
koa.alt: Rainbow-coloured light illuminates a chimney at Koa Kogyo at night.
sources: Koa Kogyo: business and products (Japanese)
Koa Kogyo: rainbow illumination dates (Japanese)

sapporo.name: Sapporo Beer Shizuoka Brewery
sapporo.point: Look for rows of silver tanks and the star emblem. Shizuoka Bakushu, a beer sold only in Shizuoka, also comes from this brewery in Yaizu.
sapporo.alt: Rows of silver tanks at Sapporo Beer's Shizuoka Brewery.
sources: Sapporo Beer: Shizuoka Bakushu and the Shizuoka Brewery (Japanese)

kibun.name: Kibun Foods Shizuoka Factory
kibun.point: Kibun's emblem peeps above a row of red roofs. The factory makes kamaboko and chikuwa fish cakes; the production-site code “+S” on its products identifies this place.
kibun.alt: A white tower with Kibun's red emblem and name rises among low red roofs.
kibun.location: Beside the Oi River railway bridge. Ajinomoto's buildings are on the opposite side of the train.
sources: Kibun Foods: the Shizuoka Factory's production-site code (Japanese)
Shimada business guide: products made at Kibun's Shizuoka Factory (Japanese)

nestle.name: Nestlé Japan Shimada Factory
nestle.point: As the wide riverbed opens up, look toward the hills. The Shimada Factory makes coffee and also uses spent coffee grounds as fuel for its boilers.
nestle.alt: Buildings marked Nestlé and NESCAFÉ stand beyond the Oi River's broad bed, with hills behind them.
nestle.location: Look upstream from the Oi River bridge. The factory is about 1.3 km from the tracks.
sources: Nestlé Japan: coffee production at the Shimada Factory (Japanese)
Nestlé Japan: using spent coffee grounds at Shimada (Japanese)

ajinomoto.name: Ajinomoto Food Manufacturing and Ajinomoto Bakery
ajinomoto.hook: Rice porridge and bread yet to bake
ajinomoto.point: The Knorr name stands out on a curved white wall. At this address are Ajinomoto Food Manufacturing's Shizuoka Factory, which makes rice porridge, and Ajinomoto Bakery's Shimada site, which makes frozen bread dough.
ajinomoto.alt: The Knorr name and red Ajinomoto emblem appear on a curved white wall.
ajinomoto.location: Near the Oi River railway bridge, across the tracks from Kibun's red-marked tower.
ajinomoto.note: The photo identifies the site's exterior. Which production lines occupy the individual buildings has not been confirmed.
sources: Ajinomoto Food Manufacturing: products made at the Shizuoka Factory (Japanese)
Ajinomoto Bakery: frozen bread dough production (Japanese)
Ajinomoto Bakery: the Shimada site's address (Japanese)

shiseido.name: Shiseido Kakegawa Factory
shiseido.hook: Make-up beneath a long white roof
shiseido.point: A broad white roof stretches along the tracks. This factory makes make-up products; the roof protects outgoing products from rain, wind and sunlight.
shiseido.alt: The long white roof of Shiseido's Kakegawa Factory runs beside the Shinkansen tracks.
sources: Shiseido: Kakegawa Factory (Japanese)
Fujita: design of the Kakegawa Factory S Line (Japanese)

marudai.name: Marudai Food Shizuoka Factory
marudai.point: A red Marudai Food emblem rises above the trees, with round windows below it. In 2023, the company featured long wiener sausages made here. The factory's code on packaging is “+P”.
marudai.alt: A large red Marudai Food emblem tops a grey building with rows of round windows.
marudai.location: About 4 km from Kakegawa Station toward Hamamatsu. Toward Shin-Osaka, it comes after Shiseido.
sources: Marudai Food: factories and production-site codes, updated July 2026 (Japanese)
Marudai Food: long wiener sausages made at the Shizuoka Factory, 2023 (Japanese)

pola.name: POLA Chemical Industries Fukuroi Factory
pola.hook: Your own train in the glass
pola.point: Watch the long glass façade of this cosmetics factory. When the light is right, you may see the Shinkansen you are riding reflected in it.
pola.alt: A Shinkansen is reflected in the long glass façade of POLA Chemical Industries' Fukuroi Factory.
sources: POLA Chemical Industries: initiatives at the Fukuroi Factory (Japanese)

pocari.name: Otsuka Pharmaceutical Fukuroi Factory
pocari.hook: A blue wall says Pocari Sweat
pocari.point: A large blue wall marked POCARI SWEAT beyond a green lawn makes this factory easy to spot. It produces drinks including Pocari Sweat.
pocari.alt: A blue POCARI SWEAT wall beyond the lawn at Otsuka Pharmaceutical's Fukuroi Factory.
pocari.related: More about the Pocari Sweat factory
sources: Otsuka Pharmaceutical: products made at the Fukuroi Factory (Japanese)

nitto.name: Nitto Kogyo Kakegawa Factory
nitto.point: Look for NITO and Nitto Kogyo's name on a white wall. The small cabinets made here are enclosures that house and protect electrical equipment.
nitto.alt: Large NITO lettering and Nitto Kogyo's Japanese name on a white factory wall.
sources: Nitto Kogyo: main products of the Kakegawa Factory (Japanese)

unicharm.name: Unicharm Products Shizuoka Factory
unicharm.hook: The familiar emblem, in the garden too
unicharm.point: Follow the yellow and orange waves along the white wall, then look for a large emblem in the garden. This factory makes baby and adult nappies, sanitary products, cleaning wipes and more.
unicharm.alt: Yellow and orange waves cross a white wall, with a large blue-and-yellow emblem in the garden in front.
unicharm.location: About 4 km from Kakegawa Station toward Hamamatsu. Toward Shin-Osaka, it comes after Nitto Kogyo.
sources: Unicharm Products: Shizuoka Factory (Japanese)
Kakegawa City: products made at the Shizuoka Factory, 2026 (Japanese)

house.name: House Foods Shizuoka Factory
house.hook: Curry, stew and a crunchy snack
house.point: Look for the tower bearing House Foods' name. This factory in Fukuroi makes Vermont Curry, Hokkaido Stew and Tongari Corn snacks.
house.alt: House Foods' white sign tower, solar panels on the lawn and factory buildings behind them.
house.related: See the nearby Shippei mascot sign
sources: House Foods: Shizuoka Factory (Japanese)
House Foods Group: products made at the Shizuoka Factory, 2024 (Japanese)

yamaha.name: Yamaha Motor Fukuroi South Factory
yamaha.hook: From the railway to the world's seas
yamaha.point: Look for red YAMAHA letters and white vertical fins. This factory makes outboard motors: engines fitted to the back of a boat.
yamaha.alt: White vertical fins and red YAMAHA lettering at Yamaha Motor's Fukuroi South Factory.
sources: Yamaha Motor: outboard motor production sites (Japanese)
Takenaka: architecture of the Fukuroi South Factory (Japanese)

teibow.name: Teibow Head Office Factory
teibow.hook: From felt hats to pen tips
teibow.point: The green TEIBOW sign marks the headquarters and factory of a company whose expertise in processing hat felt led it into making pen tips.
teibow.alt: Large green TEIBOW letters on a factory roof, alongside a vertical sign in Japanese.
teibow.note: The current allocation of individual product types to this factory has not been confirmed.
sources: Teibow: head office factory, business and history (Japanese)

suzuki-takatsuka.name: Suzuki Headquarters, Takatsuka
suzuki-takatsuka.hook: A red S above the rooftops
suzuki-takatsuka.point: The red S familiar from Suzuki cars appears above the houses. This is the company's headquarters. Motorcycle-engine production, once based at Takatsuka, moved to Miyakoda in Hamamatsu in 2018.
suzuki-takatsuka.alt: Suzuki's headquarters buildings beyond Hamamatsu rooftops, with a red S and SUZUKI MOTOR CORP. on top.
suzuki-takatsuka.location: Near JR Takatsuka Station, between Hamamatsu Station and Lake Hamana. Before the lake toward Shin-Osaka; after it toward Tokyo.
suzuki-takatsuka.related: See Lake Hamana from the train too
sources: Suzuki: current headquarters functions at Takatsuka (Japanese)
Suzuki: end of production at the former Takatsuka Factory and its relocation (Japanese)
Suzuki: Takatsuka Factory operations until July 2018, in the 2019 report (Japanese)

sinfonia.name: Sinfonia Technology Toyohashi Works
sinfonia.hook: A careful journey for silicon wafers
sinfonia.point: Beyond the lawn, the long wall reads “Toyohashi Works” and “Founded in 1917”. This is a major factory for equipment that moves thin silicon wafers cleanly through the manufacture of chips used in smartphones and other devices.
sinfonia.alt: A long factory building beyond a lawn, with the English company name and Japanese signs reading Toyohashi Works and Founded in 1917.
sinfonia.location: Miya-cho, Toyohashi, on the Tokyo side of Futagawa Station. Before Toyohashi toward Shin-Osaka; after leaving Toyohashi toward Tokyo.
sinfonia.note: The same company name can be seen about 800 m south of Nagoya Station. That is a roughly 70 m advertisement on the wall of the Market Square Sasashima shopping complex.
sources: Sinfonia: semiconductor handling equipment and Toyohashi Works (Japanese)
Sinfonia: Toyohashi Works beside the Shinkansen (Japanese)
Sogo Hodo: the roughly 70 m sign in Sasashima, Nagoya (Japanese)
Chuden Clavis: the advertisement on Sasashima's east wall (Japanese)

yamazaki-pan.name: Yamazaki Baking Anjo Factory
yamazaki-pan.point: A sun emblem and large red Yamazaki name appear close to the train. Near Mikawa-Anjo, this factory makes bread and Japanese- and Western-style sweets.
yamazaki-pan.alt: A large red Yamazaki sign at the Anjo Factory, with delivery vehicles lined up in front.
sources: Yamazaki Baking: Anjo Factory production and official recruitment information (Japanese)

nichiban.name: Nichiban Anjo Factory
nichiban.hook: A familiar sign, a changing role
nichiban.point: The red, white and blue Cellotape sign is easy to recognise. This adhesive-tape factory has also broadened its role into products that support medical care.
nichiban.alt: A large Cellotape advertisement on the red, white and blue wall of Nichiban's Anjo Factory.
nichiban.note: The 2026 facilities information lists adhesive tapes for medical support, plus paper and plastic tapes. A 2025 company statement says Cellotape-related production was consolidated in Saitama. The sign alone does not establish that Cellotape is currently made at Anjo.
sources: Nichiban: 2026 annual securities report, p. 37 (Japanese)
Nichiban: explanation of production restructuring, 2025 (Japanese)
Nichiban: the wall advertisement visible from the train (Japanese)

kirin.name: Kirin Beer Nagoya Brewery
kirin.hook: Tanks like giant glasses of beer
kirin.point: Rows of tanks are painted silver and gold. Look beyond Nagoya toward Shin-Osaka for this brewery in Kiyosu, where Kirin Ichiban is made.
kirin.alt: Silver-and-gold tanks and a red KIRIN sign at the Nagoya Brewery.
sources: Kirin: Ichiban and its breweries in 2026 (Japanese)

yanmar.name: Yanmar Research and Development Center
yanmar.hook: A large clock just beyond Maibara
yanmar.point: A long building carries red YANMAR letters and a large clock. This is the company's central research facility in Maibara, studying engine fuel efficiency and alternative energy.
yanmar.alt: Red YANMAR lettering and a digital clock at the right end of a building in twilight.
yanmar.location: Just after Maibara toward Shin-Osaka: one account records the view about a minute after departure on a Kodama. Toward Tokyo, look before reaching Maibara.
yanmar.related: See Maibara's high-speed test trains too
sources: Yanmar: fundamental research at the Maibara centre (Japanese)
Yanmar: location of the central research facility (Japanese)
Train journey account: the research centre from a Kodama's A-seat side (Japanese)

fujitec.name: Fujitec Big Wing
fujitec.hook: Where everyday ups and downs begin
fujitec.point: The tall tower is used for elevator research. Factories on the same site make standard and custom elevators, bringing research and production together.
fujitec.alt: An elevator research tower rises in front of a building bearing the FUJITEC name.
sources: Fujitec: research and production at Big Wing (Japanese)

lotte.name: Lotte Shiga Factory
lotte.hook: Sweets on a very large scale
lotte.point: Large signs show sweets and ice creams. The factory makes products including Yukimi Daifuku ice-cream mochi, Coolish and Toppo. Not every product pictured on the signs is made here.
lotte.alt: Large signs for sweets and ice creams on buildings at Lotte's Shiga Factory.
sources: Lotte: products made at the Shiga Factory (Japanese)

nissin.name: Nissin Foods Shiga Factory
nissin.hook: Instant rice comes from here too
nissin.point: Look for the Nissin Foods building in Ritto. It also makes instant rice meals such as Curry Meshi. This is a separate factory from the Kansai Factory across the tracks on the E-seat side.
nissin.alt: A building bearing Nissin Foods' name at the Shiga Factory in Ritto.
sources: Nissin Foods: the Shiga Factory's cup-rice production line (Japanese)
Nissin Foods: factory list (Japanese)

yamazaki.name: Suntory Yamazaki Distillery
yamazaki.hook: Whisky's home at the foot of the hills
yamazaki.point: Look beyond rooftops and overhead wires for the Yamazaki name. This distillery makes the malt whisky used in Yamazaki single malt.
yamazaki.alt: The Yamazaki name and SINCE 1923 on buildings at the foot of wooded hills.
sources: Suntory: Yamazaki whisky and its distillery (Japanese)

bridgestone.name: Bridgestone Hikone Plant
bridgestone.location: Takamiya-cho, Hikone, about 9 km from Maibara Station toward Kyoto.
bridgestone.point: Behind the trees, this plant makes tyres for passenger cars and light trucks. Zelkova woodland has been reported visible from the train. We are checking whether today's views let you identify the factory buildings or the giant tyre within the grounds.
sources: Bridgestone: products made at the Hikone Plant (Japanese)
Factory visit account: zelkova trees seen from the train, 2014 (Japanese)
Hikone City: rice fields between the factory and the Shinkansen (Japanese)

lion.name: Lion Odawara Factory
lion.location: About 5 km from Odawara Station toward Tokyo.
lion.point: This factory makes Systema and Clinica toothpaste. A green building appears in the book's train-window photograph. We still need to check how much can be seen over today's noise barriers.
sources: Lion: Odawara Factory guide (Japanese)
Lion: products made at the Odawara Factory (Japanese)

pg.name: P&G Shiga Plant
pg.location: Kamiya, Yasu, about 300 m from the tracks on the Lake Biwa side.
pg.point: The cosmetics made beside these fields are SK-II. We are checking whether the factory building shown in the book's train-window photograph can still be identified from passing trains.
sources: P&G: the Shiga Plant and SK-II production (Japanese)

suzuki-kosai.name: Suzuki Kosai Plant
suzuki-kosai.location: Shirasuka, Kosai, on the Toyohashi side of Lake Hamana. After Bentenjima's torii gate toward Shin-Osaka; before the gate toward Tokyo.
suzuki-kosai.point: This plant makes cars including the Alto and Spacia. Its wind turbines provide a landmark, with a 2025 photographic record from the train's A-seat side.
suzuki-kosai.note: The photo link leads to the photographer's account of their train journey. The generating equipment's operating status in 2026 has not been confirmed.
sources: Suzuki: models made at the Kosai Plant (Japanese)
Suzuki: wind-power equipment at the Kosai Plant (Japanese)
